correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Cotanvilque–Totatolani headward opening
correspondence.finding: The northern chosen opening and southward hook follow the blue headwater course west of Calacoilo/Nacatuta and through the Totatolani–Pajotane setting on the original map. The source supplies ordinary corridor correspondence; it does not justify assigning a precise spring or treating the full selected headward part as a lake. The opening is not inferred from basin membership alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Pajotane–Quequesane/Jarumas waterbody and outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected southward continuation follows the mapped stream into the blue waterbody labelled QUEQUESANE beside Vilaque/Jarumas; the map shows a dam symbol at its southern end and the continued stream below. The selected entry, through-waterbody and outlet corridor are supported. PET independently places the Jarumas dam in the upper Ticalaco basin. Quequesane and Jarumas are retained as map/locality and reservoir references, not asserted to be formally registered interchangeable names.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: upper Río Ticalaco system with Jarumas reservoir

correspondence.component_scope: Upper valley past Añaque, Trabalaco, Tucumbaya and Ticaco/Tarata toward Pistala
correspondence.finding: The original map continuously carries the chosen southward course from the dam, its westward bend through the Añaque–Trabalaco/Tucumbaya setting, and the downstream Ticaco/Tarata valley to the east–west receiving corridor around Pistala/Lukacha. All selected internal part boundaries in this interval stay on that mapped corridor at regional scale. The report distinguishes local Ticalaco, Tarata and Pistala rivers; PET identifies Ticalaco and Pistala among the courses forming Tala. No exact name-transition point or single upstream scalar is imposed.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Río Ticalaco / Río Pistala reaches, bounded naming scope

correspondence.component_scope: Pistala–Chucatamani, northern tributary join, Chipispaya and Coropuro
correspondence.finding: The source map follows the selected westward valley through Chucatamani, shows the northern tributary connection, and continues through Chipispaya/Putina to Coropuro and the westward canyon. INGEMMET field prose identifies Tala at Chucatamani and Sama below the Tala–Salado confluence; PET places that confluence downstream of Chucatamani and describes the constricted course at Chipispaya. These observations support the meaningful tributary join and the downstream representative identity without forcing Tala onto all headwater reaches.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Río Tala upstream reach; Río Sama downstream representative identity

correspondence.component_scope: Sama canyon and middle agricultural valley
correspondence.finding: The map continuously tracks the selected southwest turn below Coropuro, then the southward Sama valley past Palanca/Sambalay Grande, Agua de Milagros, Coruca, Yarascay/Argandoñas, Luco, Charañal and Yarahuay to Sama Grande. The adjacent tributary mouths are visible joining the chosen valley; nearby desert quebradas remain separate. Every selected part in this interval has ordinary corridor correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Sama Grande–Tomasiri/Las Yaras–Cuilona/La Morena lower valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen course continues through the original mapped Sama Grande and Poquera–La Banda corridor, crosses the transport corridor near Tomasiri/Las Yaras and follows the explicitly labelled Sama reach toward Cuilona, El Golpe, La Morena and Amopaya. The source separates the western Honda drainage and eastern quebradas from the selected Sama course.

correspondence.component_scope: La Vituña/Angola–Los Baños–Boca del Río actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The original blue river continues beyond the lower-valley tributary convergence past La Vituña and Angola, through the Los Baños coastal approach, and reaches the Pacific coast at Boca del Río. The selected last four parts and actual terminal are matched to this river mouth, rather than to a nearby quebrada or settlement label alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southeastern opening, Vaca Seca upper bends and all tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the mapped Quebrada Vaca Seca branch, rather than beyond an unviewed head. Direct MMA attributes label its westward upper bends and subsequent northward valley as Quebrada Vaca Seca. Every selected part and intervening junction is exposed. Short angular offsets are treated at ordinary corridor scale and do not establish exact banks.

correspondence.component_scope: Vaca Seca junction, named Salitral bend and succeeding western turn
correspondence.finding: The north end of Vaca Seca joins the westward reach carrying the direct Quebrada Salitral attributes. The selected part follows that named reach around the westward bend. The junction is exposed by the original linework; Salitral is retained as a distinct reach name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest turn and westward connecting reach into Algarrobal
correspondence.finding: MMA maps the southwest and westward channel sequence and its successive side-channel joins into the reach labeled Quebrada Algarrobal. Several connecting features have blank name attributes. Their geographic connection is supported, but no Salitral, Vaca Seca or Totoral name is assigned to those blank-name portions by inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Algarrobal northward and northwestern valley before the strand departure
correspondence.finding: MMA directly labels the western turn and long north-to-northwest trunk Quebrada Algarrobal; IGM independently publishes the same named watercourse as Q. Algarrobal over the middle stretch. The ordinary valley sequence and joins are exposed. The selected rendering runs approximately parallel to the source in parts 13–14, and these offsets alone are not treated as a bank-level failure. Geographic support here ends at the subsequent departure toward the eastern strand, separately recorded below.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: The ending of part 15 is excluded from this completed component and belongs to the following unresolved transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Departure from the Algarrobal–Boquerón trunk onto an eastern unnamed strand
correspondence.finding: Both official line publications expose the actual selected northward transfer. Their named Algarrobal trunk feeds the western Q. Boqueron/Quebrada Boquerón channel. The selected line instead leaves that trunk northward and reaches a separate eastern unnamed branch that joins the western channel farther north. Neither original depicts the selected link between these strands. This is a change of mapped branch and join sequence, rather than a request for exact banks or vertex agreement. No lake, reservoir, glacier, managed transfer or positively identified non-river feature explains this selected connector in the inspected originals.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern unnamed channel after the unresolved departure and its return to Boquerón
correspondence.finding: After the unresolved transfer, the selected northwestward reach follows the ordinary corridor of eastern unnamed natural-watercourse strands and their return to the Boquerón trunk. Both publications expose this downstream join. Blank attributes are retained as unnamed source segments, and the Boquerón name is not automatically carried over them.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Only the downstream portion of part 16 after reaching the eastern branch is covered here; its preceding transfer remains pending.

correspondence.component_scope: Boquerón/Baquerón lower bend through the Totoral junction
correspondence.finding: The northward and then northwestern lower trunk is directly named Quebrada Boquerón in MMA and Q. Boqueron in IGM. One MMA downstream segment spells the downstream reach Quebrada Baquerón. That source spelling is preserved rather than silently normalized as a formal alias. The original linework shows this branch meeting the Totoral receiving course; the selected route takes the downstream western continuation.

correspondence.component_scope: Totoral confluence, lower valley and approach to Caleta Totoral wetland
correspondence.finding: The complete westward lower-course sequence carries the direct MMA name Quebrada Del Totoral; IGM uses Q. del Totoral. Each selected lower part and intervening tributary join is exposed through the wetland approach. The independent MMA wetland inventory identifies the two receiving coastal polygons as Humedal Caleta Totoral. The mapped channel reaches this wetland setting. This supports the receiving reach identity but does not turn the wetland or all upstream branches into the same named river.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: The final northwestward extension in part 32 is excluded and treated separately below.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected northwestern ending beyond the mapped wetland/channel termination
correspondence.finding: The bounded originals cover the actual selected endpoint. The source channel approaches and terminates in the Caleta Totoral wetland setting, while the final selected segment turns northwest beyond the mapped channel and wetland polygons. No through-channel, receiving-water polygon or established overland/managed connector is depicted to the actual selected end. The wetland name alone does not prove that last through-link. Present water level, precise shoreline and current flow are not required or asserted; the remaining issue is the identity and connection of the final extension at ordinary geographic scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and headward feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies on an unnamed mapped feeder in the upper Caribou Creek valley. The source channel joins the directly labelled Caribou Creek corridor before the route proceeds south and southeast. The chosen model opening is not asserted to be the official or ultimate source of Caribou Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Caribou Creek upper and middle corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated direct Caribou Creek labels, the connected valley and readable intermediate joins support the selected upper corridor through the Glass/Mazuma/Whistle, Chitna/Billy, Divide/Sheep/Alfred and Bitter/Fortress settings. The selected route follows Caribou Creek rather than the tributaries named for geographic orientation.

correspondence.component_scope: Caribou Creek to Matanuska River junction
correspondence.finding: Caribou Creek passes the West End Creek setting and Glenn Highway, then joins the directly labelled Matanuska River by Lion Head. The selected route turns west along the Matanuska valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Glacier-side and upper Matanuska corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the Matanuska River north of the mapped glacier forefield. Glacier Creek is a mapped side connection to the river; the selected opening does not require an ice traverse or a glacier-to-river through-link. Nearby lakes are not selected through-lake passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Matanuska valley and major joins
correspondence.finding: Repeated Matanuska River labels and continuous mapped river-valley geometry cover the westward reach, including Hicks/Pinochle/Lake, Purinton/Cascade, Chickaloon and Kings River joining settings. Coarse selected segments locally cut bends or sit beside the mapped braid belt; exact channel/bank registration is not required or asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Sutton–Palmer and lower branching approach
correspondence.finding: The named Matanuska corridor continues past Granite/Eska/Moose and Wolverine tributary settings to Palmer and the lower branching floodplain. The maps distinguish Palmer Slough, the Matanuska channels and neighboring Knik River. These observations supply lower-corridor context but do not establish the final western marsh extension.

correspondence.component_scope: Final Glenn Highway crossing, western marsh extension and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selected terminal is in the wetland west of Glenn Highway, north of the mapped Matanuska main channel. The final selected westward and northwestward continuation is not followed by a continuous mapped waterway. This is a material connector gap, not a requirement to match an exact bank vertex or prove present discharge. No continuous river through the marsh, precise mouth, tidal channel, managed diversion or lake connector is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Cahuanana–El Zapote opening
correspondence.finding: Both originals show the small drainage south of Metlatónoc/Cahuanana turning east and northeast toward El Zapote and then southeast into the El Jicaral junction setting. This is the selected western feeder. The north-arriving Carrizal approach is a different branch, and the Encajonado network farther southwest is not substituted for the selected opening.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: No direct hydronym is assigned to the chosen initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: El Jicaral–La Trinidad–San Miguel Tejalpan upper trunk
correspondence.finding: The mapped eastern junction near El Jicaral leads south past La Trinidad, east of the Rancho Viejo/Yoloxóchitl settlements, and through the San Miguel Tejalpan junction. The selected valley then follows the Guerrero–Oaxaca border southward beside San José de las Flores and the Cerro Bronco/San Vicente Piñas setting. The complementary originals expose the continuous selected corridor and eastern joining approaches despite the overprinted state boundary.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The technical account supplies Carrizal/Verde regional trunk context, but these names are not forced onto the entire selected headward fragment or an exact transition point.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern border bend, Arroyo Gente and Zacacoalpan handover
correspondence.finding: The southbound mapped trunk receives the eastern San Vicente Piñas/Atotonilco-side approach, bends southwest, and continues west along Arroyo Gente and the Zacacoalpan/Plan Juste corridor. The FID10561-to10562 handover lies on this continuing valley, rather than on the separate Cortijo drainage farther south. The north-arriving San Pedro-side channel joins the trunk farther west in the Ometepec approach.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: No exact naming boundary at the modeled fragment handover is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Ometepec southern corridor to El Terrero
correspondence.finding: The selected westward reach passes south of Cochoapa and Ometepec, turns southwest along El Limón/Piedra Labrada, bends south around the Tierra Blanca/El Charco Seco setting, and returns northwest toward the main junction near El Terrero and Cerro de las Tablas. Oaxaca directly labels Santa Catarina on this selected trunk. The Guerrero original independently shows the same channel, bends and joins.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: El Charco Seco is an adjoining mapped waterbody, not an alias or an established selected lake crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate Quetzalapa–Igualapa–San Juan de los Llanos tributary
correspondence.finding: The selected tributary begins on the mapped southern Quetzalapa channel, continues past La Victoria and west of Igualapa through the El Macahuite/La Reforma setting, and reaches San Juan de los Llanos. It proceeds along the broad lower channel east of Laguna Grande into the Santa Catarina junction. The official technical description identifies Quetzala as the tributary entering this trunk downstream of San Pedro.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Quetzalapa is a settlement label; the river name Quetzala is supported by the technical hydrology account in conjunction with the mapped geographic relationship. Laguna Grande is adjacent and is not promoted to a selected lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Quetzala confluence and lower mainstem handover
correspondence.finding: The originals show the east-arriving mainstem looping by El Terrero, meeting the north-arriving Quetzala near the lower broad-channel/wetland setting, and continuing west past Cerro de las Tablas and Colonia Miguel Alemán Valdés. This accounts for the FID10562/10563 handover and the terminal join of FID10564.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The broad channel, associated side arms and nearby waters are treated as a mapped junction corridor; no present lake extent or reservoir operation is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Santa Catarina, Cortijo approach and actual Pacific endpoint
correspondence.finding: The Guerrero original directly labels Santa Catarina along the westward lower river past Colonia Miguel Alemán Valdés and follows it through the final bend to the Pacific beside Barra de Tecoanapa. The south/east-arriving Cuajinicuilapa–Barajillas channel and lower coastal joining setting are separately mapped; the technical account identifies the downstream Cortijo contribution. The selected endpoint belongs to this coastal river-mouth corridor. It is not extended to Laguna Corralero, the more southerly El Bordón waters, or a different mouth.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Oaxaca ends near the western edge of this terminal area; the Guerrero original supplies the entire actual endpoint. No exact present shoreline or mouth vertex is claimed.

bounded_primary_prose.observation: The government study calls Ometepec locally Santa Catarina. It relates the Carrizal/Verde and eastern Santa Catarina formers, then the downstream San Pedro, Quetzala and Cortijo contributions before the Pacific. This supports representative receiving-system identity and named tributary relationships. It does not make the chosen western opening the official source, fix name-transition vertices, or name every selected fragment.
